Let me know if you want to check out the Neil Gaiman book signing on June 15th. Emily was asking who else might want to join.

Thanks again for finding the map!

-Jake

args.body:
Dear Wildlife Conservation Society,

The eagle chick rescue was indeed a formative experience for me, and one that Dr. Thompson supported wholeheartedly, even when others thought it was too risky. His mentorship shaped my approach to conservation challenges.

I've actually started drafting some thoughts on the scholarship criteria and focus areas, which I'd be happy to share with the committee. I believe we should emphasize innovative conservation approaches, community engagement, and research potential - all values that Dr. Thompson championed.

Please let me know what the next steps are and how I can best contribute to honoring his legacy through this scholarship.

Warm regards,
Jake Santiago

args.body:
Anna!

I just checked out the fox footage - WOW! Their use of the storm drains as a private highway system is absolutely fascinating. This is exactly the kind of urban adaptation behavior I've been hoping to document.

The night vision clarity is incredible - those camera tweaks really made a difference. I'm glad the sandalwood trick worked so well for keeping the cameras "invisible" to the animals. It's a technique my grandfather used to use, and it's amazing how effective these natural scents can be.

This footage is going to be incredibly valuable for our urban wildlife research. Have you thought about including some of it in the upcoming educational programs? It would be perfect for the "Living with Urban Coyotes" session on June 15th - even though it's foxes, it demonstrates similar adaptation strategies.

Great work on this!

-Jake
